static_traits.name: Li Jing
static_traits.family_status: Living with parents and younger siblings
static_traits.social_status: Relationship with dance team teammates strained due to insufficient confidence; has a few close friends to confide in but they do not fully understand team pressure
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; has not yet received psychotherapy or counseling before
static_traits.language_features: Expresses clearly, fairly logical, highly cooperative, able to identify and discuss negative thinking; Low mood but Positive attitude, willing to try new approaches

basic_info.main_problem: I feel terrible at sports because I always sit on the bench when competing on the competitive dance team. This sense of inadequacy started after joining the dance team last year and has worsened as I remain unable to move up from the bench, especially noticeable during training and competitions, draining my motivation.
basic_info.core_demands: These feelings of inadequacy keep affecting my self-esteem and overall enjoyment of dance team activities, so I decided to seek counseling; I am willing to try anything that might help, hoping to boost confidence and experience by challenging negative labels and reframing perspectives.
growth_experiences: After joining the competitive dance team last year, sat on the bench long-term during competitions. Stress was moderate at first, but as I remained unable to move up from the bench, the feeling of 'I am not good enough, never getting to play' gradually emerged and worsened. Noticeably lost motivation in training and competitions; relationship with teammates strained due to insufficient confidence; although Academic performance stable with a few close friends to confide in, they do not fully understand the pressure from the dance team. To change this, doubled practice and actively sought the coach's feedback, yet emotions and self-evaluation have not yet improved.

special_situations.event: During a dance team competition, assigned to sit on the bench watching teammates perform
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot get to play, it proves I am not good enough and terrible at sports
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Proves herself by doubling practice and proactively seeking coach feedback
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am terrible; I will never get to play

special_situations.event: A move not yet done perfectly after training class
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If a move is not perfect, it means I do not deserve to play and will never get better
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Pursues perfection, practices extra, and reproaches oneself harshly

special_situations.event: Still not getting playing opportunities after receiving the coach's advice and feedback
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If effort and feedback still bring no change, it means I have no hope and am just not good enough
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Keeps practicing but ignores existing progress and focuses only on negative results
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am just not capable; no matter how much I do it is useless

special_situations.event: Relationship tension when interacting with teammates
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If there is Relationship tension, it means I am dragging the team down and disappointing others
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Reduces communication with teammates and lowers participation to avoid being evaluated
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: They think I am not good enough and look down on me

core_conflict.wish: Longs to be recognized and accepted, to be seen in the team and get to play and show oneself
core_conflict.fear: Fear of being negated and excluded, worrying that 'not being good enough' will be exposed, feeling ashamed
defense_goal: Striving for recognition through self-Demands and doubled practice, reducing Anxiety
Reduces participation and expectations to avoid public failure and shame

object_relations.self_representation: Not good enough, a marginalized bench player
object_relations.object_representation: Harshly judgmental others who only look at performance (coach / teammates)

manifestations: In training and competitions, feels a lack of meaning and hope due to long-term bench-sitting
Overall decreased enjoyment of dance team activities
Reduced motivation to participate in other activities
Close friends do not fully understand the dance team's pressure

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'. Language manifestations include: 'I must/should...', 'Everyone is like this', and so on.
manifestations: Treating 'playing = good enough, not playing = not good enough' as an absolute standard
Measures training performance by 'must be perfect'
'Never getting better' and other rigid self-evaluations emerge

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Excessive self-criticism; ignores progress and records only negative performance
Reduced participation in other activities due to Self-doubt

contact_model.definition: The individual attributes feelings they find hard to accept to others, corresponding to 'possession'. Language manifestations include: 'He is looking down on me', 'They want to exclude me', and so on.
manifestations: Attributing the self-feeling of 'I am not good enough' to teammates 'looking down on me' and 'thinking I am not capable'

positive_force: Positive attitude, willing to cooperate and try new methods (restructuring, recording, self-monitoring)
Actively practices and seeks coach feedback, has motivation to improve
Academic performance is stable; has a certain degree of self-management ability
Has a few close friends to confide in, has some social support
negative_force: Overgeneralization and mental filtering; ignores the positive side
Over-relies on external evaluation (whether one plays) to define self-worth
Decreased motivation and reduced activity participation
Relationship tension with teammates, further weakening Self-efficacy

target_behavior.behavior: Intense negative self-talk during dance team training and competitions (such as 'I am not good enough / I am terrible'), accompanied by Motivation significantly declining
antecedent: Moves not perfect enough in training
Sitting on the bench during the game
target_behavior.core_reason: Directly equating playing time with self-worth, forming Self-deprecation and failure Anticipation under cognitive biases like overgeneralization, mental filtering, and negating the positive
target_behavior.function: Avoiding shame and the risk of being negated, reducing immediate emotional pain through Withdrawal
target_behavior.consequence: Declining training engagement, difficulty sustaining improvement; Relationship tension with teammates; reduced participation in other activities, further damaged self-esteem

target_behavior.behavior: Reduces participation in other activities and social interaction (avoidance)
antecedent: After setbacks on the dance team
Being in social situations where one feels 'not understood'
target_behavior.core_reason: Lowered Self-efficacy, predicting others will give negative evaluations
target_behavior.function: Avoiding possible failure and negative evaluation, reducing Anxiety
target_behavior.consequence: Declining activity participation and social quality, Increased sense of isolation, further lowered self-esteem
